Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A sharp-lapse-rate day with strong thermals but widespread low-level wind shear. No cloud development or precipitation is forecast, but cross winds limit ridge soaring at many sites during parts of the day. Thermal flying is possible at most launches, though shear and sharp thermals demand advanced pilot skills.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — cross wind all day, layer speed shear 5 mph. Brief thermal window 2pm–4pm with light wind, peak w* 388 ft/min, thermal ceiling 4680 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.7 °C/km, advanced pilots only).
  • Hallelujah: Favorable afternoon — wind swings into preferred sector from 1pm, prime 3pm–6pm; peak w* 462 ft/min, thermal ceiling 4535–5962 ft AGL. Layer speed shear 6 mph, monitor for roughness. Sharp thermals (9.9 °C/km).
  • Slide Mountain: Marginal — wind in sector through 1pm but bulk shear 25 mph and layer speed shear 5 mph. Flying window 8am–1pm; peak w* 478 ft/min, ceiling 4282 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (8.7 °C/km).
  • McClellan: Marginal — cross wind all day, layer speed shear 6 mph. Thermal window 11am–3pm; peak w* 579 ft/min, ceiling 5809 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.0 °C/km).
  • West McClellan: Favorable afternoon — wind aligns with launch 2pm–6pm; peak w* 513 ft/min, ceiling 4891 ft AGL. Layer speed shear 6 mph. Sharp thermals (9.6 °C/km).
  • Peavine Mountain: Favorable morning — wind in sector until 1pm, light speeds; peak w* 451 ft/min, ceiling 3362 ft AGL. Bulk shear 25 mph, layer speed shear 6 mph. Sharp thermals (9.0 °C/km).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable morning — wind in sector 8am–1pm; peak w* 466 ft/min, ceiling 3637 ft AGL. Layer speed shear 6 mph. Sharp thermals (9.8 °C/km).
  • Duck Hill: Unfavorable — hazardous wind shear: layer speed shear 6 mph and direction change 32°. Afternoon wind in sector but shear risk high. Sharp thermals (10.0 °C/km).
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable — weak thermals (peak w* 197 ft/min), layer speed shear 7 mph and direction change 38°. Sharp thermals (9.0 °C/km).

Hazards

  • Low-level wind shear: Speed shear ≥5 mph per layer detected at all sites; direction change ≥30° at Duck Hill (32°) and Daydreams (38°). Strong bulk shear at Slide Mountain (25 mph) and Peavine Mountain (25 mph).
  • Sharp thermals: Region-wide lapse rate 10.0 °C/km, most sites above 9 °C/km — only advanced pilots recommended.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence: Downwind of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range ridgelines as winds shift westerly in the afternoon.
  • Moderate thermal turbulence: Domain peak σw 2.2 m/s; near rough threshold at McClellan (2.0 m/s).

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
